To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FlhD(4C) is a master regulator of flagellar gene expression in enterobacteria.
the master flagellar regulator FlhD-C directly activates transcription of a wider regulons of non-flagella genes in E. coli.
the FlhD2-C2 master regulator of E. coli flagellar gene expression binds to and activates transcription from promoters of non-flagellar, as well as flagellar, genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biogenesis and assembly of bacterial flagella, the molecular motors that drive the swimming of bacteria.
the regulation of flagellar gene expression in the enterobacteria, and in particular with the FlhD2 C2 master regulator of the class II flagellar operons.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate gene transcription in Escherichia Coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FlhD( 2)C( 2) regulates the flagella class II genes and also a subset of other genes, but that the extent and nature of this regulation is still to be fully elucidated.
FlhD( 2)C( 2) activates all the class II flagellar operons and also activates the four non-flagellar operons, b1904, gltI, wzz(f epE ) and b2446.
FlhD2/C2 is an activator that binds to DNA and regulates gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FlhD(3)C(3) is a transcriptional activator of flagellar genes and that FlhD2(2)C2(2) is a transcription activator of flagellin genes.
the FlhD2 C2 master regulator binds and activates the promoters of all eight class II flagellar operons, and in addition activates the promoters of 39 nonflagellar operons.
the FlhD2-C2 protein is a master regulator of the flagellar gene hierarchy and that this hierarchy is the core of the FlhC2-D2 regulon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FlhD2 C2 is a transcription factor with a wide range of target genes.

the FlhD2/C2 master regulator controls the expression of genes that are required to produce flagella, and that FlhD2/ C2 is not only required to produce flagellar filaments, but is also involved in the production of the flagellum-specific proteins.

FlhD( 2 )C( 2 ) is not a specific regulator of flagellum biogenesis, but rather it is a general transcriptional activator in E. coli that is able to regulate genes that have no obvious link to the biogenesis of perifrichous flagella.
